newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may miss IMF budget goals - central banker.
newsitem.headline: Russia may miss IMF budget goals - central banker.

text.p: Russia will fulfil the IMF's monetary goals by January 1 but probably not meet budget revenue targets for 1996, Sergei Aleksashenko, first deputy chairman of the central bank, said on Tuesday.
"All indicators of the monetary programme (agreed with the International Monetary Fund) will be fulfilled by January 1," he said in an interview with the daily Izvestia.
But he added that Russia was unlikely to fulfil income targets agreed with the IMF as a condition for a $10 billion, three-year loan to Russia.

"It is likely that the income side will not be fulfilled," he said. "In December we had to collect 35 trillion roubles. Real collections were maybe 20 trillion. We hope the IMF will be a bit lenient with that indicator."

Twice this year the IMF delayed payments of the Extended Fund Facility because of concerns over low tax collection -- Russia collected just 74 percent of budgeted revenues in the first nine months, though revenues improved in October and November.

The IMF resumed lending in mid-December and released one $336 million delayed tranche but has not yet signalled when it will release another delayed tranche and what will happen to money due for December.
Aleksashenko said that pressure from the IMF was understandable given the contradictory nature, at times, of Russian economic policy.
"We ourselves do not know what kind of policy will be carried out tomorrow," he told Izvestia, defending the IMF's close scrutiny.
"All our economic policy is thrown together spontaneously."
